model_interpretation.claim: The only measured unroll candidate so far—two 8-character groups—was correct but slower than baseline (82.32 µs versus 55.00 µs mean). This contrasting four-group schedule computes each group’s table lookups before validating the group, then validates all four before writing output. It may expose more independent lookup work and amortize loop control, but code size and register pressure may make it slower still. No speedup is assumed.

model_interpretation.claim: A scalar two-group unroll can expose independent table lookups to the processor and halve loop-control frequency relative to a single eight-character group. Requiring 20 remaining characters reads only the two complete groups while leaving a quartet for scalar padding/tail handling. There are no candidate timings yet; the baseline is correct at about 55.0 µs mean, and h01's two-group attempt failed to build because line separators were emitted as literal escape sequences.

items.subject: Scalar table-loop unrolling
items.objective: In its own research branch, modify only src/candidate.cpp to test scalar scheduling improvements to the existing table-driven eight-character/six-byte decode loop: unroll multiple independent groups so table lookups can overlap and loop overhead is amortized. Keep this a scalar-focused contrast to the SIMD trees; do not add explicit SIMD or parallel execution. Preserve exact output semantics, safe tails/padding, and the threads budget. Validate empty and short strings, lengths around the unrolled-group boundary, every padding case, random valid inputs, and the official Lena input before repeated native timing. Do not specialize to the benchmark length; record unsuccessful unroll/group-size choices and results.
